articles.title: Hopwood Hall College partners with Rochdale AFC for new football course
articles.excerpt: Hopwood Hall College has announced a partnership with Rochdale AFC to offer a new BTEC Sport with Football qualification starting in September 2027, providing students with unique opportunities in the football industry.
articles.content_html:
Hopwood Hall College has teamed up with Rochdale AFC to launch a new BTEC Sport with Football qualification, set to begin in September 2027.

This initiative aims to cultivate a new generation of talent for the football industry, providing students with practical training and educational opportunities.

Students enrolling in this programme will benefit from weekly training sessions led by professional coaches from Rochdale AFC. They will also have the chance to attend one free game each term at the Crown Oil Arena, further enhancing their connection to the sport.

The partnership is expected to bolster the college's boys' and girls' football teams, paving the way for greater success on the pitch.

Key figures involved in this initiative include Kris Robinson, Director of Curriculum at Hopwood Hall College, and George Delves, Head of Football Operations and Administration at Rochdale AFC.

As the programme develops, it will provide young people passionate about football with exciting new pathways into the industry.

evidence_sources.captured_text: Hopwood Hall College partners with Rochdale AFC for football course | Roch Valley Radio On Air Live now — track details aren't available right now Listen Live Watch Hopwood Hall College partners with Rochdale AFC for football course David Murphy News Editor November 10, 2026 | 4 hours ago Print Hopwood Hall College's Kris Robinson (Director of Curriculum), Zoe Staniczenko (Director of Curriculum for Sport) and Bex Cox (Curriculum Manager for Sport) Students at Hopwood Hall College will receive weekly training from Rochdale AFC coaches through a new partnership starting in September 2027. The college’s BTEC Sport with Football qualification will be delivered with the club at its Middleton Campus. Students enrolling on the course will have the opportunity to attend one free match each term at Crown Oil Arena and play a fixture at the stadium at the end of each season. The partnership covers the college’s boys’ and girls’ football teams. Rochdale AFC’s scholars have also begun taking lessons at Hopwood Hall’s Middleton Campus, where facilities include a floodlit 3G pitch and four grass pitches. Julia Heap OBE, principal and chief executive of Hopwood Hall College, said: “We’re delighted to be working alongside Rochdale AFC and are very excited about what this partnership means for young people who are pursuing their passion for football. “The club shares our ambition for nurturing local talent and ensuring they’re able to perform at the top of their game right here in Rochdale.” Laura Thomas, chief executive of Rochdale AFC, said: “This is an exciting partnership for Rochdale AFC and one that allows us to continue making a positive impact in our local community. “The Club’s owners, the Ogden Family, are incredibly passionate about the future of Rochdale as a town, and providing this opportunity for young people is an important step in that future.” Kris Robinson, director of curriculum at Hopwood Hall College, said the college had wanted to develop a partnership with Rochdale AFC since its Football Academy was established in 2000. The college’s girls’ team has won the AOC Northwest Regional League South 9-a-side competition, according to director of curriculum for sport Zoe Staniczenko.
